meta.name: Diabetic Emergency with Trauma — Hypoglycemic Driver, Single-Vehicle Crash

history.hpi: Bystanders report the patient's sedan drifted off the road at low speed and struck a mailbox post. On EMS arrival he is confused, diaphoretic, and repeating himself, with a small laceration to his forehead consistent with striking the steering wheel. A neighbor reached the patient's wife by phone, who confirms he is an insulin-dependent diabetic and skipped lunch today.
medications: Insulin lispro sliding scale with meals
history.lastOralIntake: Coffee only this morning; missed lunch
history.events: Single-vehicle, low-speed crash into a mailbox post; bystanders called 911 after finding the patient confused in the driver's seat

scene.dispatch: 54-year-old male, single-vehicle crash, patient confused, low-speed impact
scene.location: Residential street; sedan with front-end damage against a mailbox post
scene.safety: Vehicle powered off, no fuel leak, scene secured by bystanders holding traffic
scene.bystanders: Two neighbors witnessed the crash and called 911; one reached the patient's wife by phone
visualCues: Sedan front bumper crumpled against mailbox post, low-speed damage
Small laceration to forehead with minor bleeding, consistent with steering wheel contact
Patient diaphoretic and confused, still seated in driver's seat
Glucose meter visible in center console; no insulin pump present

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 54-year-old male restrained in the driver's seat of a low-speed crash vehicle. He is diaphoretic, confused, and repeating himself, with a small forehead laceration. Mechanism and presentation raise both a metabolic and a traumatic differential.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, skin diaphoretic and pale
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Moves all four extremities spontaneously, no lateralizing weakness noted
otherFindings: Small forehead laceration with minor oozing, no depressed segment palpated
Diaphoresis out of proportion to ambient temperature
Repeats the same questions, unable to state the date
Seatbelt sign across chest, no obvious deformity
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I don't... where am I going? I already told you that."

transitions.if: Primary survey done, BGL checked, dextrose given
transitions.condition: Crew performs a MARCH primary survey with spinal precautions given the crash mechanism, checks blood glucose alongside the trauma workup, and treats the discovered hypoglycemia with IV dextrose while continuing head injury monitoring.

phases.name: Primary survey done, BGL checked, dextrose given
phases.description: Crew completes a MARCH primary survey with spinal motion restriction, applies high-flow oxygen as a precaution for the head injury, checks blood glucose (32 mg/dL), and administers IV dextrose. Mental status begins improving but the crew continues treating this as a combined metabolic-and-trauma patient rather than assuming resolution.
phases.triggerCondition: After the primary survey identifies no massive hemorrhage or airway compromise, the crew checks blood glucose given the diaphoresis and confusion, finds it critically low at 32 mg/dL, and administers IV dextrose while maintaining spinal precautions and head-injury monitoring for the crash mechanism.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Patent, speech clearer but still mildly confused
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, skin drying, improved color
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Moves all four extremities spontaneously, strength symmetric
otherFindings: Forehead laceration dressed, no expanding hematoma
Cervical collar and spinal motion restriction in place
Answering orientation questions correctly but slowly
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Okay... I think I get it now. My sugar must have dropped."

expectedActions.shortAction: Perform MARCH primary survey with spinal precautions before treating suspected hypoglycemia
expectedActions.rationale: The crash mechanism requires ruling out life threats before attributing the presentation solely to a metabolic cause.

expectedActions.shortAction: Check point-of-care blood glucose given diaphoresis and confusion after the crash
expectedActions.rationale: Diaphoresis and confusion after a low-speed crash should prompt a glucose check rather than assuming trauma alone explains the mentation.

expectedActions.shortAction: Dextrose 10% IV in incremental doses (up to 250 mL / 25 g total) until mental status improves
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Unconscious patient, or patients who are unable to protect their own airway: Dextrose IV – administer in incremental doses until mental status improves or maximum field dosing is reached (if available, D10% is preferred). Maximum field adult dosing: 25 g of 10–50% dextrose IV: 250 mL of 10% dextrose
expectedActions.rationale: Incremental dosing corrects the hypoglycemia while avoiding overshoot hyperglycemia.

expectedActions.shortAction: Apply high-flow oxygen via non-rebreather as a precaution for the head injury
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer high-flow oxygen via NRB (non-rebreather) as a precaution against unanticipated deterioration
expectedActions.rationale: Precautionary oxygenation protects against unanticipated deterioration from the head injury.

expectedActions.shortAction: Monitor blood pressure closely; target SBP ≥110 mmHg given the head injury
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Blood pressure: avoid hypotension. Adult (age greater than 10 years): maintain SBP greater than or equal to 110 mmHg
expectedActions.rationale: Hypotension worsens cerebral perfusion in a patient with a possible traumatic brain injury.

transitions.if: Mental status normalizes, neuro monitoring continued
transitions.condition: Blood glucose normalizes and mental status returns toward baseline; the crew continues serial neurologic reassessment en route rather than assuming the head injury workup is complete simply because the hypoglycemia resolved.

transitions.if: AMS blamed on trauma alone, BGL not rechecked
transitions.condition: The crew attributes any persistent confusion solely to the head injury and does not recheck blood glucose, allowing recurrent hypoglycemia to go uncorrected and mimic a worsening traumatic brain injury.

phases.name: Mental status normalizes, neuro monitoring continued
phases.description: The patient's mental status returns to baseline after dextrose correction. The crew transports for head injury evaluation despite the resolved hypoglycemia, since the crash mechanism and forehead laceration still warrant a trauma workup.
phases.triggerCondition: After dextrose correction restores normal mental status, the crew recognizes the head injury still requires evaluation and continues serial neurologic reassessment and transport rather than downgrading the call now that the sugar is corrected.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, skin warm and dry
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Moves all four extremities spontaneously, strength symmetric, no focal deficit
otherFindings: Fully oriented to person, place, time, and event
Recalls missing lunch and taking his morning insulin
Forehead laceration stable, no new bruising or swelling
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "That's so much better. I really need to eat something before my shift ends next time."

expectedActions.shortAction: Continue serial neuro reassessment en route despite resolved hypoglycemia
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Patients with traumatic brain injury may deteriorate as intracranial swelling and hemorrhage increase.
expectedActions.rationale: A corrected glucose does not rule out an evolving intracranial injury from the crash.

expectedActions.shortAction: Transport to an appropriate facility per field triage guideline given the head injury mechanism
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Decisions regarding transport destination should be based on the ACS-COT 2022 National Guideline for the Field Triage of Injured Patients
expectedActions.rationale: The crash mechanism and forehead laceration still warrant trauma-capable evaluation regardless of the resolved hypoglycemia.

phases.name: AMS blamed on trauma alone, BGL not rechecked
phases.description: The crew treats the confusion as purely trauma-related and does not recheck blood glucose. The hypoglycemia recurs and worsens, mimicking an expanding intracranial injury and delaying the correct treatment.
phases.triggerCondition: The crew assumes the initial confusion was fully explained by the head injury and does not recheck blood glucose after the first dose of dextrose wears off, so recurrent hypoglycemia is mistaken for a worsening traumatic brain injury.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Patent but sluggish, minimal verbal response
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, skin diaphoretic and cool
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Withdraws to painful stimuli only, no clear lateralizing weakness
otherFindings: Mental status has worsened rather than trended toward baseline
No new pupillary asymmetry or posturing to suggest herniation

expectedActions.shortAction: Recheck blood glucose given persistent AMS; treat recurrent hypoglycemia rather than assuming isolated TBI deterioration
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Repeat check of blood glucose level if previous hypoglycemia and mental status has not returned to normal
expectedActions.rationale: Worsening mentation without new lateralizing signs or hypotension should prompt reconsidering the metabolic cause, not just the trauma.
